references.text: The original instruction for the courtyard hangings, pillars, sockets, and all accessories fulfilled in Exodus 39:40.
Repeats the list of the courtyard hangings, pillars, sockets, gate curtain, pegs, and cords as materials to be gathered.
Describes the actual making of the courtyard hangings, pillars, sockets, and all equipment now presented in Exodus 39:40.
Moses is commanded to set up the courtyard around the tabernacle and hang the curtain for the gate of the courtyard.
The completion of the task where Moses sets up the courtyard and hangs the curtain for the gate.
The responsibility of the Gershonites included the courtyard hangings, the entrance curtain, and the cords—the same equipment mentioned here.
Describes the service of the Gershonites with the courtyard hangings, the curtain, and the cords of the tabernacle.
Connects the command to make the courtyard equipment with the actual completion of these elements.
Links the physical components of the courtyard directly to the Levites' specific responsibility to carry and maintain them.
Confirms the completion of the same structural elements (sockets and pegs) mentioned in the source verse.
Connects the command to make the pegs and cords with the later finished list of equipment.
Links the physical components of the courtyard directly to the Levites' responsibility to carry them during service.
